newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: South African firm suspends ostrich auctions.
newsitem.headline: South African firm suspends ostrich auctions.

text.p: A South African auction company said on Tuesday it had suspended auctions of ostriches due to a string of setbacks that have hit the industry in recent months.
"Congo Fever is only one of the many setbacks that the ostrich business is battling with at the moment," said Koos van Rensburg, auctions manager at Seeff Holdings.

The European Union has temporarily barred imports of South African ostrich meat due to an outbreak of the haemorrhagic fever among workers at an ostrich abattoir in Oudtshoorn, capital of the country's ostrich industry, last month.
In August several farms in the area were hit by outbreaks of Newcastle disease, a sickness affecting poultry. In recent weeks hundreds of ostriches have been killed by floods in the district.

"The suspension of auctions is effectively a measure to protect the ostrich business in that the birds are not sold at a loss which might have resulted in a collapse of the market," van Rensburg said.
"Ostrich buyers are not certain about the immediate demand for ostriches and are therefore cautious. Under these circumstances it makes no sense to go ahead with auctions."
Van Rensburg said Seeff was one of the biggest ostrich auctioneers in Africa, but gave no figures.
